problem: Audio-visual navigation policies are trained end-to-end with RL and transfer poorly to real robots; the only prior sim2real effort (SonicVerse) uses plain data augmentation and ignores that the acoustic sim2real gap varies with frequency.
motivation: Ray-tracing acoustic simulators are less accurate at low frequencies due to wave effects, so models that treat all frequencies as equally reliable degrade on real audio. A modular design with a supervised high-level prediction task also lets the sim2real gap be measured on collected real data without running a robot.
key_idea: Predict a local sound-pressure field (acoustic field prediction) around the agent, and at test time pick the frequency sub-band that combines lowest measured sim2real error with highest received energy, then navigate to the field peak with a waypoint planner.
insight: Sim2real error does not decrease monotonically with frequency, so the best band is not simply the highest one, and the best band for white noise does not suit all sounds. On real data, Best-freq AFP barely helps (distance 0.74 vs 0.74 for all-freq) while Highest-energy AFP gives 0.70 and combining both (FA-AFP) gives 0.63, showing both cues matter. The hierarchical design also matters for real transfer: end-to-end DDPPO failed all real trials.
method: Acoustic Field Prediction (AFP): from a 128x128 depth image and 1 s binaural audio, predict the top-down L×L (9×9, 0.5 m resolution) sound-pressure field. A ResNet visual encoder and a 2D-conv STFT audio encoder are tiled and concatenated, then a linear layer outputs the field; trained with MSE.
Simulated acoustic-field dataset: SoundSpaces 2.0 RIRs computed on an L×L grid per receiver, with pressure taken as the max RIR amplitude; 1.1M/52K/52K train/val/test samples from Matterport3D.

Hierarchical navigation: take the field peak as the long-term goal (updated when a new peak is larger), plan with FMM on an on-the-fly occupancy map (BFS for non-navigable goals), and stop when the peak is at the field center.
Sim2real gap measurement: train per-sub-band AFP models (N=5 bands) in simulation and test on real white-noise field data to obtain per-band errors e_i.
Frequency-adaptive selection: weight w(i)=(1/e_i)^α · (r_i/r_max)^β (α=5, β=0.8 from grid search) and use the band with the highest weight for prediction.
Real robot deployment: Hello Robot with a 3Dio binaural mic; the robot's low-frequency noise is added as training augmentation, and the robot stops to resample audio at each long-term goal.

setting.backbone: ResNet (pretrained) + 2D-conv audio encoder for AFP, trained in simulation; FMM planner
setting.training_data: 1.1M simulated acoustic-field samples (500 episodes × 57 Matterport3D training scenes) from SoundSpaces 2.0; 73 sounds for training the frequency-adaptive model; robot-noise augmentation for real deployment
setting.observation: egocentric depth 128x128 + 1 s binaural audio (mono-averaged for real data); occupancy map built from depth
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT / STOP, driven by predicted long-term goals with an FMM planner (Hello Robot navigation stack on the real robot)

results: On Continuous AudioGoal, AFP reaches SR 0.91 / SPL 0.76 / SoftSPL 0.75, beating the strongest baseline DDPPO (0.82 / 0.63 / 0.66). On real acoustic field data FA-AFP reduces distance error to 0.63 vs 0.74 for All-freq AFP, and on a real robot it succeeds in 75% of 20 trials while DDPPO failed all.
limitations: Validation and test real data were collected in the same environment, so generalization to new acoustic environments is untested.
Real evaluation is small (20 robot trials, 7 sounds × 10 points at coarse 3×3 resolution).
